SHW.rationale: Sherwin-Williams is a high-quality franchise with dominant market position (69.4% US Paint Stores industry share), strong brand, and vertically integrated distribution moat. Q1 2026 results showed solid execution: revenue +6.8% YoY, EPS +7.5% YoY, gross margin expanded 90bps, and all three segments grew. The company reaffirmed 2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $11.50-$11.90. However, several factors temper enthusiasm: (1) Q1 is seasonally weak and QoQ metrics show significant sequential decline (revenue -10.9%, EPS -35.8%), (2) operating cash flow was only $139M vs $1.31B in Q3 2025, reflecting seasonal working capital build, (3) debt-to-equity of 2.1x is elevated, (4) raw material inflation guidance was raised to low-to-mid single digits with Middle East supply risks, (5) volume guidance was moderated with some areas potentially declining low single digits, and (6) DIY demand remains persistently soft. Valuation at PE 30.7x is near the low end of its 365-day range (29.4-37.1), suggesting the market has partially priced in the cautious outlook, but it is not cheap enough to compensate for the muted growth trajectory. The 7% price increase for PSG effective Jan 2026 and BPA regulatory tailwind in packaging provide modest near-term support, but these are already reflected in guidance. Net-net: solid franchise, fair-to-slightly-cheap valuation, but growth is modest and headwinds are real.
